name: Diesel; combusted in industrial boiler
description: Provides an estimated national mix of industrial diesel boiler combustion technologies in the US. Size shares use oil-product capacity shares from an assessment of stationary combustion technology in the US (Schoeneberger et al. 2022).

processDocumentation.timeDescription: Mix year 2017, based on the equipment inventory vintage used in an assessment of stationary combustion technology in the US (Schoeneberger et al. 2022) and related national inventory data.
processDocumentation.geographyDescription: Based on US facility reported data.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: US average mix of industrial diesel boilers. Capacity shares: 1 percent less than 10 million Btu per hour (uncontrolled), 25 percent from 10 to 100 million Btu per hour, and 74 percent greater than 100 million Btu per hour (low NOx burners), based on oil-product capacity shares from an assessment of stationary combustion technology in the US (Schoeneberger et al. 2022).
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: Mix of NETL unit processes already in the US Life Cycle Inventory. Small boilers (less than 10 million Btu per hour) use the uncontrolled inventory; many units in that size class fall below NSPS Subpart Dc coverage for steam generating units. The mid-size bin has no low NOx burner inventory in the database, so the uncontrolled mid-size inventory is used. Large boilers (greater than 100 million Btu per hour) use low NOx burners. Control technology is not reported in the size inventory used for mix shares, so low NOx burners for large units are a documented technology choice for an unspecified national average, consistent with NSPS Subpart Db expectations for combustion controls on large steam generating units and with EPA AP-42 guidance that low NOx burners are among the most common NOx controls on fuel-fired boilers. Selective catalytic and non-catalytic reduction and flue gas recirculation unit processes are excluded from this unspecified average (add-on controls are not assumed for the national average).
processDocumentation.restrictionsDescription: All information can be accessed by everybody.
